title: Minimax Robust Regret for Ordinal Outcomes at Positive-Mass Multicategory Ties
banked_reason: D0.5.G: exact all-selector minimax equality and count-rule attainment are proved only for a tailored local subclass; paper_score_ceiling 6.7 < field threshold 7.4.
gap_reasons: The exact all-selector minimax equality and count-rule attainment are proved only for a tailored local subclass in which one prespecified stratum varies while every nonfocal outcome law is tangent-invariant and separated by a fixed action gap; for larger observational classes the note delivers only the converse.

The every-radius non-minimaxity result for the raw direct plug-in is qualitative: the balanced centered probability is not certified away from 5/9, so the normalized small-radius gap may vanish, and the proposed moderate-radius quantitative separation remains open.

The framing accurately limits these claims, but the narrow prespecified-tie experiment, lack of quantitative evidence for the comparator gap, and prospective-only application keep the package below a leading-journal headline despite the delivered sharp local characterization.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived a sound sharp local minimax equality, count-rule attainment, and qualitative raw plug-in comparison for a one-tie, nonfocal-invariant observational subclass. Independent mathematical and rubric reviews passed, but the cold novelty review capped the delivered package at subfield because the larger observational class receives only a converse and the quantitative calibration remains incomplete. A field-tier re-raise needs a broader experiment with a new upper-bound construction or a concrete application, not another review of this scope.
tldr: At a positive-mass five-category ordinal leaf where the sharp transportation faces and the two deterministic robust actions tie, the project characterizes first-order minimax expected excess worst-case oracle regret by an eight-dimensional Gaussian decision game. On the declared nonfocal-invariant subclass, a total covariance-adapted count selector attains the game value uniformly over the compact design class. The raw Zhang--Luo--He direct plug-in rule is strictly non-minimax at every finite positive radius. If \(p_0(q,e)=P_{N(0,\Sigma(q,e))}\{\widetilde h(Z)>0\}\), its exact small-radius coefficient is \(\max\{5(1-p_0),4p_0\}\), whereas the minimax coefficient is \(20/9\). The resulting normalized gap is nonnegative and is positive exactly when \(p_0\ne5/9\). No auditable rational bound separating the balanced value \(p_0(1/2,1/2)\) from \(5/9\) is claimed; that computation and the moderate-radius gap are optional calibrations, not premises of the every-radius strict comparison.
gap: ZhangLuoHe2026, equation (6), equation (8), Section 6.1, and Table 1 provide a raw direct plug-in implementation as well as a distinct smoothed orthogonal estimator, sharp ordinal bounds, and a no-tie upper rate. The paper does not derive the raw rule's local Gaussian law or minimax regret at a positive-mass simultaneous-face tie. Tetenov2012 settles shifted thresholds for classical asymmetric treatment experiments, while Kido2023 and MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local settle adjacent Gaussian reductions under different risk orders; none contains this ordinal score or its global partial-hyperplane obstruction. Finite-game algorithms do not control continuous eight-dimensional discretization, random estimated covariance, or outward-rounded rational separation at \(q=e=1/2\) of \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{ZLH},H_0}^{\mathrm{bal}}\) from \(V_{H_0}(1/2,1/2)\) for a fixed \(H_0\in[1/4,1]\).
fill: The project distinguishes the global observation score \(\widetilde h\) from its parameter restriction \(h\), proves the raw Zhang--Luo--He direct plug-in rule converges to \(\mathbf 1\{\widetilde h(Z)>0\}\), establishes an all-selector Gaussian minimax equality and count-based attainment, and uses the global partial-hyperplane obstruction to prove a strict every-radius regret advantage for the calibrated count rule. Its open computational target fixes \(q=e=1/2\) and requires a rational \(H_0\in[1/4,1]\) with outward-rounded rational bounds that strictly separate \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{ZLH},H_0}^{\mathrm{bal}}\) from \(V_{H_0}(1/2,1/2)\).
